tasks.short: Collect labour market and workforce benchmarks for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.

today.trigger: A recurring benchmark update or a question from HR about recruitment, pay or workforce availability.
steps: Find relevant CBS, UWV, sector and purchased reports.
Download tables and extract figures from reports.
Align occupations, regions, periods and definitions with Noordhaven's workforce.
Record sources and dates, then save a benchmark table for analysis.
drudgery: Checking the same sources for updates.
Copying figures and repairing table formats.
Tracing figures back to their definitions.
today.time_sinks: Estimated baseline: 77.9 hours/year. Most effort goes into finding updates and making differently defined figures comparable.

lenses.faster: Scheduled downloads replace repeated browsing and copying. Extraction drafts include the source, period, unit and definition beside each figure.
lenses.autonomous: Approved structured sources refresh on a schedule; failed downloads, changed schemas and unfamiliar definitions enter an exception queue.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a regional evidence base for warehouse and transport hiring instead of assembling benchmarks only when someone asks.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet repair and repeated searching, leaving time to judge whether a benchmark actually fits Noordhaven.
lenses.options: Compare regional, sector and occupation benchmarks side by side, showing differences rather than choosing one convenient number.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the source catalogue, comparison rules and quality checks instead of collecting every release.
reach: Recruiter: regional hiring-market briefings.
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: preparation of external pay benchmarks.
FP&A Analyst: external workforce assumptions for planning.

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a benchmark represents shift workers, drivers, office staff or agency workers sufficiently well to inform a decision.
tasks.pattern_why: Most recurring collection can use scheduled downloads and explicit validation rules. An optional llm_step extracts tables from narrative reports, with source checks before acceptance.

in_practice.trigger: A scheduled source check detects a new release.
steps: Retrieve approved public datasets or permitted purchased files using a scheduled script.
Validate structure, units, reporting periods and regional coverage.
Normalize accepted records; route report-extraction drafts and definition changes to the analyst.
Refresh the benchmark table and publish its source dates and exceptions.
in_practice.human_gate: Approve new sources, changed definitions and extracted report figures; established structured feeds run without approval each time.
systems: Approved public APIs and licensed downloads
data_needed: Source catalogue with access and reuse conditions.
Occupation, region and sector mappings.
Reference periods, units and revision markers.
Accepted benchmark definitions and validation tolerances.
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint source register recording release dates, retrieval results, validation failures and accepted revisions.

evidence.claim: CBS provides API access to current StatLine datasets, supporting scheduled collection of approved tables.
A 75% recurring time reduction is a pilot estimate assuming stable sources; initial setup and maintenance are additional.

risks: Regional or sector averages may poorly represent Noordhaven's jobs and shift patterns.
Revisions and changed dataset structures can silently break comparisons.
Purchased reports may restrict automated extraction or redistribution.
research_questions: Which sources account for most of the current 77.9 hours, and do they permit automated access?
Can existing benchmarks be mapped consistently to Noordhaven's occupations and three locations?
Over three releases, how many records require manual correction or interpretation?

tasks.short: Tell HR and managers what changed in dashboards, reports and metric definitions.

today.trigger: A report, tool or metric definition changes.
steps: Compare the old and new versions and identify affected users.
Write an explanation with links and examples.
Update SharePoint guidance and distribute the announcement through Teams or Outlook.
Answer questions and correct misunderstandings.
drudgery: Updating the same explanation in several places.
today.time_sinks: Estimated baseline: 75.9 hours/year. Repeated drafting, audience selection and follow-up questions consume more time than sending announcements.

lenses.faster: Generate a release note, manager explanation and FAQ from one approved change record.
lenses.autonomous: An approved release triggers distribution to registered report owners and audiences, with delivery failures routed back.
lenses.ambitious: Give each affected audience a short explanation of how a change affects its decisions and comparisons.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive announcements and link maintenance, leaving useful conversations about how managers use the information.
lenses.options: Draft a short alert, a worked example and a detailed explanation so the analyst can choose the right format.
lenses.altitude: The analyst designs the release and communication process and monitors whether users understand changes.
reach: HR Administrator: maintenance of HR reporting guidance.
L&D Specialist: short learning materials for dashboard users.
Controller: communication of shared HR-finance metric changes.

tasks.human_edge: Explaining sensitive changes honestly and spotting when a message could be interpreted as criticism of a site or manager.
tasks.pattern_why: The workflow combines change comparison, drafting, audience selection and publication. Approval is needed because a misleading definition announcement can change management decisions.

in_practice.trigger: A report owner submits a completed change record for release.
steps: Collect the approved change, affected reports and registered audiences.
Draft plain-English release notes and role-specific examples using approved source material.
Check links, dates, access permissions and consistency with the metric dictionary.
Present the publication package for approval, then distribute and record delivery.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves each communication package; the HR Director approves messages with material policy implications.
systems: Proposed Power Automate approval and distribution flow
data_needed: Versioned change records and metric definitions.
Report ownership and audience lists.
Approved examples and communication templates.
Access groups and publication destinations.
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint release register containing the approved text, source version, approver and distribution results.

evidence.claim: SharePoint and Power Automate support document approval workflows; tailored drafting and distribution would require configuration.
A 65% recurring time reduction is plausible when changes are documented consistently; it is not a measured Noordhaven result.

risks: A generated explanation may alter the meaning of a metric.
Announcements or examples may expose employee information to an overly broad audience.
Office communication channels may miss shift supervisors who need the update.
research_questions: Do releases currently contain enough structured information to generate accurate explanations?
Which audiences need different explanations or delivery channels?
Does a pilot reduce clarification requests without reducing understanding?

tasks.short: Write clear specifications for HR dashboards, reports and their data.

today.trigger: HR, Finance or a site manager requests a new report or a significant change.
steps: Clarify the decision, audience and reporting frequency.
Inspect available AFAS, Recruitee or Studytube fields and existing definitions.
Document calculations, joins, filters, access rules and output layout.
Agree acceptance examples and obtain the report owner's sign-off.
today.time_sinks: Estimated baseline: 72.7 hours/year. Ambiguous definitions, missing fields and repeated review rounds cause most delay.

lenses.faster: Turn request notes and verified model metadata into a first specification, including missing decisions and acceptance examples.
lenses.autonomous: A new request starts a draft and completeness check; unresolved definitions remain assigned questions.
lenses.ambitious: Specify every important HR metric with its owner, lineage, permitted audience and known limitations.
lenses.joy: Remove template filling and repeated field descriptions, leaving the analyst to resolve what the business actually needs.
lenses.options: Compare a simple report using current data with richer versions requiring new capture or integration.
lenses.altitude: The analyst maintains specification standards and reusable metric definitions rather than drafting every document from scratch.
reach: HR Business Partner: translating workforce questions into measurable requirements.
Controller: shared definitions for headcount, FTE and labour cost.
L&D Specialist: requirements for certificate and onboarding reporting.

tasks.human_edge: Resolving conflicting interests and agreeing what 'productive after 90 days' means for different jobs without creating intrusive monitoring.
tasks.pattern_why: A draft can combine requests, metadata and existing definitions, but business meaning, access and acceptance criteria require explicit agreement.

in_practice.trigger: A report request enters a SharePoint request list.
steps: Retrieve the request, approved dictionary and available field metadata.
Draft the purpose, population, calculations, joins, refresh timing and access rules.
Flag missing data, conflicting definitions and assumptions requiring a decision.
Generate acceptance examples, including agency workers and hires not yet observed for 90 days.
Route the specification to the analyst and accountable business owner for approval.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst checks technical feasibility; the business owner approves meaning and acceptance criteria. HR assesses applicable privacy and OR requirements before implementation.
systems: AFAS, Recruitee and Studytube export or API metadata
Proposed company-approved language model and approval workflow
data_needed: Request notes and business decision to support.
Verified field catalogue, identifiers and available history.
Metric definitions, CAO populations and worker classifications.
Access requirements and worked acceptance examples.
in_practice.logs_to: Versioned SharePoint specifications with open questions, source references, decisions and approvals.

evidence.claim: Drafting specifications from verified metadata and request notes is plausible, but semantic accuracy still needs human review.
Changes to arrangements for processing employee data can require works council consent; this must be assessed beyond document approval.

risks: The model may invent available fields or valid joins.
A precise-looking specification may conceal an unresolved business definition.
Employee and agency-worker identifiers may not support reliable historical linkage.
The specification may introduce employee monitoring requiring additional governance.
research_questions: Can current systems link vacancies, hires, onboarding and day-90 outcomes reliably?
Who owns the definitions of productivity, retention and vacancy cohorts?
Do generated specifications reduce review rounds while preserving completeness?
Which proposed outputs change employee-data arrangements or monitoring?

tasks.short: Explain workforce trends and recommend actions that improve successful hiring and retention.

today.trigger: A monthly HR review, an unexpected metric movement or a management question.
steps: Collect validated recruitment, workforce, onboarding and absence measures.
Compare trends by site, job family, cohort and worker type.
Investigate anomalies with recruiters, HR Business Partners and managers.
Prepare recommendations with evidence, caveats and proposed owners.
drudgery: Recreating the same comparisons each month.
Checking whether narrative numbers match the dashboard.
today.time_sinks: Estimated baseline: 71.3 hours/year. Repeated slicing and commentary take time, while confirming explanations requires conversations.

lenses.faster: Calculate recurring comparisons automatically and draft commentary only from checked results.
lenses.autonomous: A successful nightly refresh prepares an exception brief; recommendations remain drafts until the analyst reviews context.
lenses.ambitious: Track whether interventions improve productive, retained hires rather than merely reporting recruitment speed.
lenses.joy: Remove chart copying and number checking, leaving investigation, discussion and evaluation of practical changes.
lenses.options: Compare actions such as onboarding support, interview scheduling and shift-offer changes, with explicit assumptions and costs.
lenses.altitude: The analyst designs an evidence-and-learning cycle that connects workforce signals, decisions and measured outcomes.
reach: HR Business Partner: evaluation of retention interventions.
Recruiter: recruitment funnel diagnosis.
FP&A Analyst: workforce scenarios and intervention cost estimates.

tasks.human_edge: Separating plausible explanations from causes and choosing actions with managers who understand work on each site.
tasks.pattern_why: Trend calculations and briefing preparation are automatable, but recommendations depend on operational context, uncertainty and consequences for people.

in_practice.trigger: A validated refresh completes before the monthly HR review.
steps: Calculate agreed cohort measures and changes using deterministic queries.
Check completeness, observation windows, seasonality and minimum reporting group sizes.
Draft a brief linking each statement to a checked result and listing alternative explanations.
Develop action scenarios with costs, owners and evaluation measures.
Have the analyst investigate with managers and present the supported recommendations.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst validates interpretation and the HR Director or responsible manager decides actions; the workflow makes no individual employment decisions.
data_needed: Linked vacancy, hire, start-date and employment-end history.
Agreed productivity milestones and onboarding completion records.
Cohort maturity, shift, site and job-family information.
Intervention dates, costs and operational context.
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint analysis and decision register with query versions, evidence, assumptions, approved actions and follow-up dates.

evidence.claim: Deterministic comparisons combined with reviewed narrative drafts plausibly halve recurring preparation effort; this is unmeasured.
AI intended for recruitment or employment decisions may be high-risk; classification depends on intended use, beyond calling the tool a copilot.

risks: Associations between onboarding, shifts and retention may be presented as causal.
Small cohorts can reveal individuals or produce unstable rankings.
Hires with fewer than 90 days of observation may be incorrectly counted as failures.
Recommendations may drift into individual hiring, retention or performance scoring, requiring a fresh legal and governance assessment.
research_questions: Is productivity measured consistently enough to support the North Star?
How much preparation time remains after automating comparisons and number checks?
Can prior recommendations be evaluated against subsequent outcomes?
Can useful analysis be delivered using aggregates without individual predictive scores?

tasks.short: Test HR dashboards and data feeds against agreed definitions, source totals and user needs.

today.trigger: A new report, a changed calculation, a source-system change or a suspected reporting error.
steps: Translate agreed requirements into test cases.
Reconcile extracts and dashboard totals with source records.
Check calculations, filters, access and edge cases.
Ask report users to verify that outputs answer their questions.
Record defects, retest fixes and approve release.
drudgery: Building and documenting similar test cases.
Capturing screenshots and manually comparing totals.
today.time_sinks: Estimated baseline: 67.9 hours/year. Repeated reconciliation and retesting consume time; business acceptance depends on user availability.

lenses.faster: Run reusable reconciliation and regression checks automatically, with evidence attached to each failure.
lenses.autonomous: Each extract and report change triggers defined tests; failures block publication of an updated trusted dataset.
lenses.ambitious: Check critical HR measures after every refresh, including historical corrections, access boundaries and cohort calculations.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive arithmetic and screenshot collection, leaving investigation and conversations about whether reports support decisions.
lenses.options: Generate candidate edge cases for starters, leavers, transfers, agency conversions and overlapping absence records.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the quality framework, failure thresholds and acceptance process.
reach: Payroll Specialist: reconciliation evidence for payroll reporting.
Controller: headcount and labour-cost reconciliation checks.
HR Administrator: identification of source-data exceptions.

tasks.human_edge: Defining independent expected results and deciding whether a technically correct report answers the real business question.
tasks.pattern_why: Reconciliations, calculation checks and access tests have explicit expected outcomes. AI can help write test code, while recurring execution needs no model.

in_practice.trigger: A nightly extract completes or a report change is submitted for release.
steps: Run source-count, uniqueness, completeness and reconciliation checks.
Execute approved calculation cases covering cohort maturity, transfers and worker types.
Verify access with representative test accounts, including Power BI workspace permissions.
Record results, block failed releases and assign exceptions to the analyst.
Obtain business acceptance for new or materially changed outputs before publication.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst resolves failures and approves test changes; the report owner accepts new business behavior. Passing routine refreshes need no individual approval.
systems: Proposed SQL or Python test runner
A separate test workspace where available
data_needed: Approved specifications and independently calculated expected results.
Source control totals and extract timestamps.
Representative synthetic edge cases.
Access matrix and representative user roles.
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted test-results store with summaries and defect ownership in SharePoint, recording data and report versions.

evidence.claim: Microsoft documents separate deployment stages, supporting controlled report release; custom quality tests remain necessary.
Power BI row-level security applies to workspace Viewers; privileged workspace roles require separate attention in access testing.
A 70% recurring saving assumes reusable tests cover most current checks; setup and business acceptance remain additional work.

risks: Tests generated from the same faulty calculation may reproduce its error.
A failed refresh may leave stale data visible unless freshness is clearly displayed.
Technical checks cannot establish whether managers need a different measure.
Available Power BI licensing may limit deployment tooling.
research_questions: Which historical reporting errors would the proposed checks have caught?
Can independent source totals and expected calculation examples be obtained?
Do current licences support separate test and release environments?
What proportion of test effort is repeatable versus genuine business acceptance?

tasks.short: Compare competing employers' hiring offers and local labour market trends.

today.trigger: Hard-to-fill vacancies, falling offer acceptance or a periodic recruitment-market review.
steps: Identify competing employers and relevant public vacancies around each site.
Record advertised pay, shift patterns, benefits and entry requirements.
Compare offers with Noordhaven's terms and applicable CAO provisions.
Summarize supported differences and discuss responses with Recruitment and Compensation and Benefits.
drudgery: Separating base pay from allowances and bonuses.
today.time_sinks: Estimated baseline: 61.4 hours/year. Collection and pay normalization dominate, especially where advertisements omit hours or allowances.

lenses.faster: Extract standard fields from permitted vacancy sources and flag missing terms instead of manually rewriting advertisements.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled watch detects changed offers and prepares comparisons; uncertain pay interpretations wait for review.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a dated local view of the employment offer around all three sites and connect changes to Noordhaven's recruitment outcomes.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive browsing and allowance arithmetic, leaving discussion of which employment terms matter to applicants.
lenses.options: Compare total-package scenarios involving base pay, shifts, travel allowance, training and contract security.
lenses.altitude: The analyst designs the comparison method and evidence standards rather than maintaining a pile of vacancy screenshots.
reach: Recruiter: competitor-employer intelligence.
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: total-package comparison preparation.
FP&A Analyst: costing alternative recruitment offers.

tasks.human_edge: Recognizing that an advertised offer is incomplete evidence and judging which changes Noordhaven can realistically offer within its CAOs.
tasks.pattern_why: Collection, extraction and normalization span several sources with ambiguous terms. A person must approve interpretations and conclusions before they inform pay or recruitment decisions.

in_practice.trigger: A scheduled permitted-source check detects new or changed vacancies.
steps: Collect relevant advertisements through permitted feeds, downloads or manual uploads.
Extract job, location, hours, base pay, allowances and benefits with supporting text.
Deduplicate advertisements and calculate comparable packages using explicit rules.
Flag missing terms, unmatched jobs and uncertain CAO interpretations.
Present a sourced comparison for analyst and Compensation and Benefits review.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves the comparison; Compensation and Benefits validates pay assumptions and applicable CAO treatment before recommendations are used.
systems: Proposed collection scripts and company-approved language model
data_needed: Relevant employer, occupation and travel-area lists.
Dated advertisement snapshots or permitted excerpts.
Noordhaven pay, hours, allowances and benefits.
Current approved CAO interpretation and package-comparison rules.
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint comparison register with source dates, calculation assumptions, uncertainties and reviewer decisions.

evidence.claim: Extracting vacancy terms into a checked comparison is plausible, but source access and missing package details may limit automation.
The proposed 55% saving is a pilot assumption and does not establish that advertised offers explain recruitment outcomes.

risks: Advertised ranges may exclude allowances or describe different hours and responsibilities.
Reposted vacancies are not reliable measures of hiring volume or employer market share.
Collection may be restricted by source terms.
An unsupported CAO interpretation could distort package comparisons.
research_questions: Can enough comparable local advertisements be collected lawfully and consistently?
What share contains sufficient hours, pay and allowance detail for a defensible comparison?
Do reviewed extracted terms match manual calculations closely enough to save time?
Which offer differences do recruiters and candidate feedback identify as consequential?

tasks.short: Produce checked workforce reports for HR, Finance, management and the works council.

today.trigger: A reporting calendar deadline or an approved request for employment information.
steps: Confirm the reporting population, definitions, recipient and deadline.
Collect workforce, recruitment, learning and permitted absence data.
Reconcile records and calculate the required measures.
Prepare tables and commentary, then review access and obtain sign-off.
Distribute the approved report and retain the reporting evidence.
drudgery: Rebuilding recurring tables and presentation formats.
Checking recipient lists and repeating period-end calculations.
today.time_sinks: Estimated baseline: 58.2 hours/year. Reconciliation and manual packaging dominate; this task covers recurring production rather than new analytical investigations.

lenses.faster: Generate recurring report packs from one validated dataset and approved templates, with reconciliation evidence attached.
lenses.autonomous: Reporting deadlines trigger preparation; standard internal packs can be distributed automatically after checks under an approved reporting mandate.
lenses.ambitious: Produce consistent, traceable views for HR, Finance and the OR instead of reconciling different numbers during meetings.
lenses.joy: Remove month-end copying and formatting, leaving investigation of exceptions and useful explanations.
lenses.options: Offer approved views by site, job family and employee or agency-worker population without rebuilding the report.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the reporting catalogue, definitions, access controls and quality thresholds.
reach: HR Administrator: recurring workforce statistics.
Payroll Specialist: payroll-report reconciliation preparation.
Controller: workforce and labour-cost reporting preparation.

tasks.human_edge: Accepting accountability for a report's purpose, interpretation and permitted audience, especially where it supports formal obligations.
tasks.pattern_why: Recurring populations, calculations, reconciliations and formats can be written as explicit rules. Formal releases and material exceptions retain named human sign-off.

in_practice.trigger: A reporting-calendar deadline occurs after the nightly extract passes validation.
steps: Load approved AFAS data and separately configured exports from other systems.
Apply versioned definitions, worker-population rules and reporting-period logic.
Reconcile totals, test freshness and apply agreed disclosure controls.
Generate recipient-specific reports and route exceptions or formal submissions for approval.
Distribute permitted packs and archive the exact data snapshot and report version.
in_practice.human_gate: Routine internal packs run under approved rules; the accountable owner signs formal submissions and the analyst resolves discrepancies before release.
systems: AFAS GetConnectors or existing approved extracts
Approved Recruitee, Studytube and agency exports
data_needed: A reporting catalogue stating purpose, obligation, recipient and accountable owner.
Historical contracts, FTE, starts, exits and worker classifications.
Permitted absence dates and agreed absence definitions.
Reporting templates, access groups and reconciliation totals.
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted reporting register and archive recording source snapshots, checks, approvals, recipients and release timestamps.

evidence.claim: AFAS GetConnectors retrieve configured data definitions, providing a supported basis for controlled reporting extracts.
Employers may process limited absence information and must not process medical details such as the nature or cause of illness.
A 75% recurring saving assumes stable templates and reliable inputs; no specific statutory submission is assumed to exist or be automated.

risks: Employee payroll headcount and agency-worker deployment may be combined incorrectly.
Late corrections can change previously reported periods unless snapshots and revisions are controlled.
Absence reports may disclose medical information or identifiable small groups.
A report does not establish compliance with Wet verbetering poortwachter case obligations; case owners remain responsible.
research_questions: Which reports are genuinely required, by whom, under what obligation and with whose sign-off?
Can payroll, HR and Finance agree reconciled historical headcount and FTE definitions?
Are agency data timely enough for the intended reporting deadlines?
Can two reporting cycles run in parallel with no unexplained differences and less manual effort?

tasks.short: Keep HR reporting templates, metric definitions and reusable analysis assets current.

today.trigger: A reusable asset changes, a new asset is created or someone cannot find the current version.
steps: Collect templates, definitions and analysis examples from their owners.
Check duplicates, accuracy, permissions and current approval status.
Update files, metadata and links in SharePoint.
Archive superseded assets and tell users where the approved version lives.
today.time_sinks: Estimated baseline: 53.3 hours/year. Version cleanup, ownership checks and repeated searches consume most effort.

lenses.faster: Suggest metadata, identify duplicate candidates and prepare change summaries automatically when files enter the library.
lenses.autonomous: New versions and review dates trigger checks and owner reminders; approved assets retain a clear current-version link.
lenses.ambitious: Build a dependable HR knowledge library where every important metric and template has an owner, review date and usage example.
lenses.joy: Remove file housekeeping and reminder chasing, leaving improvement of useful standards and examples.
lenses.options: Show candidate duplicates and proposed revisions side by side so owners can choose what to retain.
lenses.altitude: The analyst designs the library's structure, ownership rules and review process.
reach: HR Administrator: template-library housekeeping.
L&D Specialist: reusable dashboard guidance.
Controller: shared workforce-definition and reporting-template maintenance.

tasks.human_edge: Deciding which asset is authoritative and recognizing when a seemingly editorial change alters policy, CAO meaning or contractual obligations.
tasks.pattern_why: Classification, comparison and reminders can be automated, but publication, replacement and archiving require owner judgment about authority and meaning.

in_practice.trigger: A file is added or changed, or its review date is reached.
steps: Read permitted files and propose owner, topic, review date and asset type.
Check links, approval status and potential duplicates using deterministic checks and text comparison.
Draft a change summary and suggested metadata or revision.
Obtain owner approval before publishing, replacing or archiving authoritative assets.
Update the catalogue and retain prior versions under the approved retention policy.
in_practice.human_gate: The asset owner approves publication and retirement; policy and contract changes remain with the responsible HR or legal owner.
systems: Proposed company-approved language model with permission-aware retrieval
data_needed: Existing assets, version histories and permissions.
Named owners, approval status and review dates.
Library taxonomy and authoritative-source rules.
Retention rules and links to approved CAO and policy sources.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint version history and a library-maintenance register recording suggestions, owner decisions and publication or archive actions.

evidence.claim: SharePoint document-library events can initiate Power Automate approval workflows.
evidence.source: [Microsoft: Trigger approvals from a SharePoint document library](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/trigger-sharepoint-library)

evidence.claim: Metadata suggestions, duplicate detection and change summaries plausibly reduce recurring maintenance effort by 65%, subject to owner response times.

risks: Similar templates may serve different CAOs or worker populations and must not be merged automatically.
A generated revision may change contractual or policy meaning.
Search or retrieval may reveal documents beyond the user's permissions.
Aggressive archiving may conflict with retention requirements or destroy useful historical context.
research_questions: How many assets lack an owner, approval status or review date?
Can duplicate suggestions distinguish genuine duplicates from legitimate CAO or population variants?
Does permission-aware retrieval preserve existing access boundaries?
Will owners approve or reject suggestions quickly enough to reduce maintenance effort?

role.altitude: The role becomes the owner of a reliable workforce evidence system: definitions, integrations, tests, reporting controls and evaluation of decisions across hire to productive, employee lifecycle, absence and payroll.
reach: Recruitment funnel and regional labour-market analysis for the recruiters.
Onboarding and certificate-reporting preparation for L&D.
Workforce and labour-cost reconciliation preparation for Payroll and the Controller.
Retention-intervention evaluation for HR Business Partners.
Workforce scenario preparation with FP&A, using approved assumptions.
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks total 538.6 hours/year, about 33.7% of the implied 1,600-hour role. The estimates release about 347 recurring hours/year, or 21.7% of the role and approximately EUR 27,000 of capacity at EUR 78/hour, before setup, maintenance, licences and review overhead; this is not cash savings. Speedups include remaining human work and automated execution but exclude initial implementation. Savings overlap unless shared collection, testing and reporting work is counted once. The existing AFAS extract is nightly, other integrations are unconfirmed, and the remaining role tasks are unassessed. Policy, individual employment decisions, medical judgment and formal payroll accountability stay with their responsible owners.
skills_to_grow: SQL, Power Query and DAX for versioned, testable workforce measures.
API and export integration, historical identity matching and data lineage.
Automated reconciliation, access testing and release control.
Cohort analysis, uncertainty, experiment design and causal interpretation.
Clear specification writing and facilitation of shared metric definitions.
AVG/GDPR data minimization, access control, retention and DPIA assessment with the privacy lead.
OR consultation and consent assessment for employee-data arrangements and monitoring.
EU AI Act intended-use assessment when analysis could influence recruitment or employment decisions.
Evaluation of model extraction and drafting against reviewed examples.
role.ambitious_version: Run a workforce learning cycle across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo: connect vacancies to starts, agreed productivity milestones and day-90 retention; identify process bottlenecks; help managers test improvements; and measure results. Agree the vacancy-cohort denominator, treatment of cancellations, repeat openings and immature hires before publishing the North Star, with employee and flex-worker populations shown explicitly. Expand from reporting what happened to evaluating which changes improve successful hiring, while applying the necessary privacy, OR and AI governance to each intended use.
